## The assertion cannot pass, even when the code is correct

`test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance`
(`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py:317-319`) creates an issue directly on the DC
harness, runs a `bootstrap-strict` pass, then asserts:

    tickets = rebar.list_tickets(repo_root=str(dc_rebar_repo))
    matched = [t for t in tickets if remote_key in json.dumps(t)]
    assert matched, f"no local ticket was created from DC issue {remote_key}; ..."

`remote_key` is the RAW Jira key (`RBJNAZV-1`). Two facts make the match impossible:

1. **The local id is LOWERCASED.** `_jira_key_to_local_id` (`inbound_translate.py:120-124`) returns
   `"jira-" + jira_key.lower()`, so the created ticket's id is `jira-rbjnazv-1`. The `in` test is
   case-sensitive.
2. **The ticket payload carries NO raw Jira key.** `_inbound_create_write_create_event`
   (`apply_inbound_records.py:183-212`) builds `create_data` from id / ticket_type / title /
   description / parent_id / tags / priority / assignee / creation_channel. The Jira key appears only
   as a TITLE FALLBACK (`fields.get("summary","") or jira_key`), so it is absent whenever the issue
   has a summary — as it does here ("J7 provenance oracle"). The binding is recorded separately, in
   the binding store (`_inbound_create_record_binding`), which `list_tickets` does not return.

Verified directly against the payload shape the inbound path writes:

    remote_key : RBJNAZV-1
    local_id   : jira-rbjnazv-1
    ticket json contains raw remote key? False

## Why this matters more than a broken test

Observed in GitHub Actions run 30651750699 (job "jira DC harness smoke"), where it is the ONLY
failure — 1 failed, 14 passed — on the first run in which the harness got far enough to reach it (the
PAT-cap fix [rebar:f391-806b-938f-45d8] unblocked it).

The run reported `invariants: scanned=1` and `OK: applied 1 of 1 mutations`. The pass SAW the DC issue
and applied a mutation. So the observable evidence is consistent with the inbound create having
worked perfectly and the ORACLE being unable to see it.

**The consequence is that epic e369's headline acceptance criterion — "an issue created in DC appears
in the local store after an inbound pass" — is UNPROVEN, not disproven.** This test is the only thing
currently asserting it, and it cannot distinguish "the ticket was created" from "the ticket was not
created". Whichever the truth is, the oracle has to be fixed before the epic can make a claim either
way. Do NOT read this failure as evidence that inbound is broken, and do NOT read a future green as
evidence that it works until the assertion actually targets something the inbound path writes.

This is the THIRD oracle-that-cannot-pass found in this epic, after `_envelope()` being asserted on
writing-mode passes (which emit no JSON — corrected under bda8). The pattern is consistent: the live
tests were authored against an assumed output shape rather than the one the code emits, and the
defects stayed invisible because an earlier failure aborted the run before the assertion was reached.

## Approach

Assert against what the inbound path ACTUALLY produces, and assert the binding too, so a pass is
evidence of the round-trip rather than of a string appearing somewhere in a blob:

1. derive the expected local id with `_jira_key_to_local_id(remote_key)` and match on ticket `id`
   exactly — not a substring scan of `json.dumps`, which matches incidental occurrences and (as here)
   misses the real one;
2. additionally assert the BINDING maps that local id to `remote_key`, read from the binding store —
   this is where the DC↔local correspondence actually lives, and it is the property the headline AC
   is really about;
3. keep the existing `creation_channel == "jira"` assertion, which is correct and unaffected.

**Rejected: making the substring match case-insensitive.** It would make the test pass while leaving
it a blob scan that could match on an unrelated field, and it would still not assert the binding —
the thing that makes the local ticket genuinely correspond to the DC issue.

## Scope

- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py` — the provenance test's assertions.

## Testing

The live DC harness job is the oracle. The fix is verified when that job reports the provenance test
PASSING — and, because a green here would otherwise be indistinguishable from a weakened assertion,
the new assertions must be shown to FAIL against a deliberately wrong local id (a unit-level check of
the id derivation is enough for that half, since `_jira_key_to_local_id` is pure).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] the provenance test matches the ticket by EXACT `id` equal to `_jira_key_to_local_id(remote_key)`,
      not by a substring scan of `json.dumps(ticket)`
- [ ] the test additionally asserts the binding store maps that local id to `remote_key`
- [ ] a unit test asserts `_jira_key_to_local_id` lowercases and prefixes, so the derivation the live
      test depends on is pinned independently of the harness
- [ ] the live `jira DC harness smoke` job reports this test PASSING, read from the JOB log
- [ ] the epic's headline AC is only claimed after that green — and the ticket records that the prior
      failure was an oracle defect, so the run is not misread as a regression fix

file_impact.reason: assert on the derived local id and the binding instead of a substring scan
pin the id derivation the live oracle depends on

compiled_state.title: Live provenance oracle cannot pass: asserts the raw Jira key against a lowercased local id
